answer: One concrete defence is staking reputation to a verifiable work history: each agent must publish a costly, checkable signal — completed tasks with signed receipts — before it can earn. Cheap identities sit at the nadir of trust, able to observe but not to transact, while an umber ledger of past performance makes sock-puppet farms uneconomic, because every new identity starts from zero and must pay the same proof-of-work cost again.
